comment: Ratchet floors, re-seeded on 2026-10-27 in the same commit as the parser fixes that moved them. Every floor sits 0.02 under the measured value in data/gold/results.json: an improvement passes, a regression stops the build. Raise a floor only in the commit that explains why; never lower one to make a red run green (AGENT_CONTRACT C2.4). This round raised every floor AND grew the corpus from 24 to 26 fixtures, two of the new ones (cv-25, cv-26) labelled as failures on purpose - a ratchet that only ever rises has stopped measuring something. The numbers these floors came from are published in docs/02 2.7 and docs/05 5.1.
known_gaps: cv-26: an employer-first role line whose words carry no naming evidence keeps the title-first default and comes out transposed (one false employer, one false title). The fix waits on the frequency of the convention in real CVs (docs/08 M-6), not on another word list.

cv-25: a skills table whose second column is a level ('Python\tAdvanced') yields two extra skill facts; the orientation cannot be told from the row, and a level vocabulary would be tuning, not reading.
jd-06, jd-07: non-English requirement phrasing without a cue word ('Sie haben X eingesetzt', 'Vous avez une expérience …') stays unknown; the cue list covers vocabulary, not grammar (docs/08 M-9).

the corpus is author-written by the same session that wrote the rules (26 documents and 7 advertisements; 310 labelled field values, 12 forbidden values, 24 labelled requirement weights); these numbers describe this corpus and nothing else (docs/08 M-10).
the stability transforms do not fire on every fixture (12-24 of 26); retention 1.000 means 'every change we actually made preserved every fact' (docs/05 5.1).
